answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity: each agent locks a deposit that is slashed if its attestations prove false, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like a violet thread woven through marble, reputation accumulates slowly and visibly across epochs, while a new account starts with velvet-soft trust that only hardens after consistent honest work. Sybils can still appear, but they cannot cheaply buy the history real peers earn.
